artist: Gestalt Girl (ゲシュタルト乙女)
title: 再見
song_form: Intro (0:00-0:31, 8 bars acoustic strum with late bass/pad swell) -> Verse 1 (0:31-0:56, 8 bars intimate acoustic + sparse bass) -> Verse 2 (0:57-1:22, 8 bars full rhythm section enters with clean arpeggios and tight drums) -> Chorus 1 (1:22-2:01, 12 bars full-band dynamic lift) -> Instrumental Interlude (2:01-2:25, 8 bars clean guitar & bell-like keys drop-down) -> Chorus 2 (2:25-3:04, 12 bars) -> Bridge (3:04-3:28, 8 bars rising harmonic tension and rhythmic build) -> Final Chorus & Tag (3:28-4:08, 12+ bars peak intensity with repeated refrain) -> Outro (4:08-4:58, stripped-back acoustic, clean arpeggios, and ringing D major decay)

instrumentation.role: Primary harmonic bed and rhythmic pulse in intro, verses, and outro; subtly glues the chorus strumming
instrumentation.tone: Bright, crisp bronze-string shimmer with clear pick transient and controlled low-mid body; close-miked natural room sheen
instrumentation.playing_style: Steady open-position 8th/16th-note strumming using D-shape open voicings with ringing add9 and sus2 extensions

instrumentation.role: Melodic arpeggios, shimmering upper-register counter-lines, and the signature interlude motif
instrumentation.tone: Glassy, chime-heavy Telecaster/Stratocaster-style clean tone with light optical compression, subtle tape/plate reverb, and zero harshness
instrumentation.playing_style: Precision picked arpeggios, diatonic dyads, and delicate upper-neck fills during verses, interlude, and outro

instrumentation.role: Chorus and bridge harmonic weight, wall-of-sound warmth, and soaring lead counter-melodies
instrumentation.tone: Warm, mid-forward tube overdrive (low-to-medium gain, Vox/Fender-amp breakup character) with smooth high-end roll-off rather than fizzy modern distortion
instrumentation.playing_style: Full open/power-chord strums in choruses layered alongside a higher-register lead guitar playing lyrical single-note and octave counter-melodies

instrumentation.role: Grounded sub-harmonic anchor that shifts from sparse sustain to driving melodic propulsion
instrumentation.tone: Round, woody P-Bass/J-Bass fingerstyle tone with warm low-mids, rolled-back clank, and gentle pick/finger attack
instrumentation.playing_style: Whole/half-note roots and fifths in Verse 1, evolving into locked 8th-note root-pushing grooves with scalar passing tones and octave turnarounds in choruses

instrumentation.role: Dynamic architecture controller—tight pocket keeper in verses/interlude, expansive wash in choruses
instrumentation.tone: Natural, slightly damped indie-rock kit: dry, punchy snare with focused 200-500 Hz body and crisp wire snap; tight, controlled kick; warm, shimmering cymbals
instrumentation.playing_style: Closed hi-hat 8th-note pocket with ghosted snare accents in Verse 2 and interlude; half-open hi-hat/ride wash, solid 2-and-4 backbeat, and melodic tom fills in choruses

instrumentation.role: Subtle atmospheric glue and delicate upper-register sparkle in the interlude and outro
instrumentation.tone: Warm Rhodes-style electric piano blended with a glassy celesta/glockenspiel-like bell attack
instrumentation.playing_style: Sustained warm chord pads in soft transitions and crisp upper-octave arpeggiated doublings over the clean guitar in the interlude and outro

guitars: Dual-layered guitar architecture balancing acoustic clarity and indie-rock electric warmth. An acoustic guitar carries open D-major voicings (rich with open B and E strings creating add9/sus2 halos) throughout the quiet sections. A single-coil clean electric guitar weaves intricate, rhythmically crisp arpeggios and upper-register melodic hooks (especially prominent in Verse 2, the 2:01 interlude, and the outro), running through light compression and modest plate reverb/short delay. In the choruses and bridge, warm tube-overdriven electric guitars enter—pushed into smooth, mid-focused breakup rather than scooped fuzz or high-gain metal—while a second electric guitar adds lyrical, delay-kissed single-note lead counter-melodies on top.
bass: Warm, rounded fingerstyle electric bass sitting cleanly beneath the guitars without metallic fret buzz. In Verse 1 it breathes with sustained whole and half notes on chord roots and occasional fifths. Once the drums enter in Verse 2 and the chorus, it shifts to steady, grounded 8th-note motion locked tightly to the kick drum, connecting chord changes via diatonic passing notes (C#, E, F#) and gentle octave jumps at 4-bar phrase boundaries.
drums: Organic, minimally processed live indie drum kit. Verse 1 is drumless; Verse 2 introduces a tight, dry pocket with steady 8th notes on closed hi-hats, a punchy damped snare on beats 2 and 4, and restrained kick patterns. Choruses expand onto crash-rides and sloshy half-open hi-hats with emphatic snare backbeats and short, musical tom fills leading into downbeats. The interlude pulls back to crisp, dry hi-hat/snare stick control before ramping up again through the bridge.
keys_and_synths: Restrained and tasteful—never dominating the rock band core. A soft electric piano/Rhodes pad provides gentle low-mid warmth during early swells, while a bright, bell-like keyboard timbre (Rhodes tine/glockenspiel hybrid) reinforces the clean electric guitar arpeggio during the 2:01 instrumental interlude and the stripped-back 4:08 outro.
harmony: Anchored firmly in D major (Ionian) with classic Japanese indie/alt-rock emotional voicings (maj7, add9, sus2, m7) that soften cadence resolutions. Verse progressions cycle smoothly through diatonic pillars such as I - V/vii (A/C#) - vi7 (Bm7) - IVmaj7 (Gmaj7) - V (A). The chorus deploys a soaring Royal Road-derived lift: IVmaj7 (Gmaj7) -> V (A) -> iii7 (F#m7) -> vi7 (Bm7) -> ii7 (Em7) -> V (A) -> I (D), creating bittersweet momentum without leaving the diatonic home key. The bridge leans into minor-tinted pre-dominant tension (Em7 - F#m7 - Gmaj7 - A) before resolving cleanly back into the final chorus.
melody: To build an instrumental melody in this style, combine a lyrical, singable upper-register lead line with interlocking clean guitar arpeggios. Melodic phrases tend to enter slightly ahead of or behind the barline (syncopated eighth-note pickups), favor stepwise scalar motion within D major pentatonic and Ionian (highlighting the 3rd F#, 5th A, and 9th E over chords), and leap expressively up a sixth or octave at chorus peaks before stepping gently down toward the tonic or 3rd.
rhythm_and_groove: A steady, unhurried 80 BPM 4/4 pulse that feels simultaneously nostalgic and driving because of continuous 8th-note subdivisions in the acoustic strumming, bass, and hi-hats. Subtle 16th-note syncopations in the acoustic strum and clean guitar picking keep the slow tempo buoyant. The groove avoids heavy funk swing or rigid quantization—it breathes naturally like a live four-piece band with subtle push into chorus downbeats.

mix_and_production.reverb_and_space: Controlled, intimate-to-medium studio space. Verses are noticeably dry and close, using short room ambience on drums and subtle plate reverb on clean guitars. Choruses open up with slightly longer hall/plate tails on lead guitar and cymbals, while still keeping the rhythm section articulate and uncluttered.
mix_and_production.distortion_and_saturation: Gentle, organic analog-style saturation. Guitars use warm amp-like overdrive with smooth midrange density; bass and drums remain clean with just enough tape/console glue to avoid sterile digital edges. Zero harsh fuzz, bitcrushing, or aggressive clipping.
mix_and_production.stereo_width: Focused center anchor (kick, snare, bass, main acoustic body) framed by wide-panned clean arpeggio guitars, stereo-spread overdriven chorus guitars, and panned drum overheads/toms. Transitions feel dramatically wider when the overdriven guitars enter on chorus downbeats.
mix_and_production.brightness_and_eq: Balanced, natural midrange warmth with crisp acoustic string sheen and clear cymbal air around 8-12 kHz, avoiding piercing 3-5 kHz harshness or sub-bass boom below 60 Hz.
mix_and_production.compression_and_loudness: Moderate, musical dynamic compression preserving transient life on acoustic strums and snare hits. Not brickwalled; clear loudness contrast exists between the quiet acoustic intro/outro, tight verses, and full-bodied choruses.
mix_and_production.dynamics_and_arrangement: Textbook Japanese indie-rock terraced dynamics: sparse acoustic opening -> full-band tight verse -> expansive overdriven chorus -> delicate clean-guitar/chime interlude drop -> climbing bridge -> soaring final chorus -> gentle acoustic/clean-arpeggio fadeout.

signature_traits: Bright, open-string D-major acoustic strumming layered seamlessly beneath indie electric guitars
J-rock 'Royal Road' (IV - V - iii - vi) chorus harmony colored with maj7 and add9 voicings
Clean single-coil electric guitar arpeggios paired with bell-like Rhodes/glockenspiel accents in breakdowns
Warm, mid-focused tube overdrive in choruses rather than heavy distortion or fuzz
Tight, dry 80 BPM drum pocket that switches smoothly to a crash-ride wash in choruses
Sharp dynamic contrast between intimate drumless/sparse passages and wide full-band peaks
what_it_is_not: Washed-out shoegaze ambient pads or cavernous infinite reverb
EDM sidechain pumping, four-on-the-floor kicks, or electronic risers
Chiptune, 8-bit synths, or glitchy hyperpop vocal/instrument chops
High-gain scooped metal distortion, djent chugs, or fuzzy stoner-rock riffs
Heavy trap hi-hat rolls or booming 808 sub-bass
Complex odd-meter math-rock time signature shifts (stays strictly in accessible 4/4)
